rows.grounds: means by which action is performed

items.question: Can an agent produce an effect without employing any instrument?
premises: Agency is ordinarily associated with producing effects.
Instruments are ordinarily required for producing effects.
A hypothetical agent acts without an instrument.
items.inference: The possibility of agency without an instrument is put in question.
items.plain_english: Could one be an agent while producing an effect without any instrument?

rows.grounds: fused form indicating something different from power

items.question: Is power alone the instrument in the bodily activities of individual selves?
premises: Nothing other than power functions as the instrument.
Individual selves engage in bodily movement and similar activities.
These activities require an instrument.
items.inference: Power alone is stated to be the instrument even for the activities of individual selves.
uncertainties: The exact referent of the editorial marker (vi0 3|4 is unclear.
items.plain_english: Thus it is said that, even in the bodily movements and other activities of individual selves, power alone is the instrument.

items.question: Can an ungrasped adjunct serve as the effect of the Lord?
premises: An adjunct may be considered even if ungrasped.
The Lord is associated with producing effects.
An effect ordinarily stands in a determinate relation to its cause.
items.inference: The status of an ungrasped adjunct as the Lord's effect is challenged.
items.plain_english: Moreover, if an adjunct is ungrasped, can it still be the Lord's effect?

items.question: How can one devoid of knowledge of the cause be an agent?
premises: Agency involves producing effects.
Knowledge of the cause is relevant to agency.
The subject is described as lacking knowledge of the cause.
items.inference: One devoid of knowledge of the cause cannot properly be an agent.
items.plain_english: Or how could this one be an agent if devoid of knowledge of the cause?

items.question: Is all existence mere blind darkness without the lamp of power?
premises: Power functions as an illuminating lamp.
Without illumination there is darkness.
The whole situation is considered in the absence of power.
items.inference: Without the lamp of power, everything would be total blind darkness.
items.plain_english: Without the lamp of power, this entire reality would be blind darkness.

items.question: How is Śambhu's power accepted as both non-different and distinct?
premises: Śambhu possesses power.
Power is accepted as not other than Śambhu.
Power is also accepted as distinct from Śambhu.
items.inference: Śambhu's power is held to be both non-different and distinct.
items.plain_english: Śambhu's power is accepted as not other than him and yet also distinct.

rows.grounds: because of a relation of essential identity
as in the case of a different self

items.question: Does identity-relation exclude difference like that between separate selves?
premises: Power stands in a relation of identity with Śambhu.
Difference like that between separate selves implies external otherness.
The text also denies that power is simply stated as different.
items.inference: Because of identity-relation, power is neither different like another self nor merely declared different.
items.plain_english: Because of the relation of identity, there is no difference as with another self; thus it is said, nor is it merely stated as different.

items.question: Why is Śambhu's power described as inherent though both non-different and distinct?
premises: Śambhu's power is not other than him.
Śambhu's power is also distinct.
Inherence explains inseparable yet distinguishable relation.
items.inference: Therefore Śambhu's power is inherent in him.
items.plain_english: Therefore, though not other and yet distinct, that power of Śambhu is inherent in him.

rows.grounds: power taken as utterly separate from his own being

items.question: Is the blessed Lord endowed with a power absolutely different from his own self?
premises: The Lord is associated with power.
Absolute difference would make power external to his own self.
The verse denies such absolute difference.
items.inference: The blessed Lord is not endowed with a power absolutely different from his own self.
items.plain_english: For this blessed Lord is not endowed with a power absolutely different from his own self.

rows.grounds: because it is observed or understood thus

items.question: Why is the Lord understood solely as endowed with consciousness-power?
premises: The Lord is observed in relation to consciousness-power.
This endowment is presented as the defining basis of understanding.
No other basis is indicated here.
items.inference: The Lord is understood precisely because of being endowed with consciousness-power.
items.plain_english: Because he is seen precisely as endowed with the power of consciousness.

items.question: Can the great Lord be the cause even without imposed particularity?
premises: Causation is often associated with particular conditions.
The great Lord is described as without imposed particularity.
The verse affirms his role as cause.
items.inference: Even without imposed particularity, the great Lord is the cause.
items.plain_english: Even without imposed particularity, the god Maheśvara is the cause.

rows.grounds: set in motion by Śiva's power

items.question: What characterizes bindu when its effects are dissolved and impelled by Śiva's power?
premises: Bindu is the subject under discussion.
Its effects are described as dissolved within it.
It is impelled by Śiva's power.
items.inference: Bindu is the state in which dissolved effects are held and moved by Śiva's power.
items.plain_english: That bindu, with its effects dissolved, is impelled by Śiva's power.

rows.grounds: having sustained the universe for long

items.question: Does bindu alone proceed after long sustaining the universe within itself?
premises: Bindu has long held the universe within it.
A principle of manifestation must proceed into activity.
The verse emphasizes bindu exclusively.
items.inference: Bindu alone proceeds after having long sustained the universe.
items.plain_english: Indeed, bindu alone, having long held the universe, proceeds forth.

rows.grounds: by clay passing into another condition

items.question: How does the analogy of clay attaining another state apply to this principle?
premises: Clay can attain another state while remaining clay.
The subject is compared to this prior example.
Change of state does not require loss of underlying nature.
items.inference: In the same way, this principle also undergoes change of state analogously to clay.
items.plain_english: Just as clay attains another state, so too does this, as before.

rows.grounds: for the sake of varied effects
in Śiva who bears the trident

items.question: Can the unchanging trident-bearer account for the difference of effects?
premises: Effects appear in different forms.
The trident-bearer is described as unchanging.
Causation must still be possible.
items.inference: Even in the unchanging trident-bearer, difference of effects is possible.
items.plain_english: Even in the unchanging trident-bearer, difference of effects is possible.

rows.grounds: of processes involving differentiation, drying, and pulverizing

items.question: What kinds of changes arise from differences in states and conditions?
premises: Difference, drying, and pulverization are named as processes.
These processes are born from differences of state.
State-difference can account for varied transformations.
items.inference: Processes like differentiation, drying, and pulverization arise from differences of state.
items.plain_english: Differentiation, drying, and pulverization arise from differences of state.

items.question: How can an unchanging possessor of power be agent of creation and other acts?
premises: Creation and other activities require an agent.
The agent is described as unchanging.
The agent is also described as possessing power.
items.inference: The unchanging possessor of power can be the agent of creation and other activities.
items.plain_english: Even while unchanging, the possessor of power is the agent of creation and other activities.

rows.grounds: source of becoming liquid and dry

items.question: How can the unchanging sun be the cause of liquidity and dryness?
premises: The sun is associated with causing liquidity and dryness.
The sun is described as unchanging.
An unchanging cause can produce varied effects.
items.inference: The sun, though unchanging, is the cause of liquidity and dryness.
items.plain_english: Even while unchanging, the sun is the cause of liquidity and dryness.

items.question: How can unchanging Śiva be the cause of bondage and liberation for individual selves?
premises: Individual selves undergo bondage and liberation.
Śiva is described as unchanging.
Śiva is affirmed as the cause of bondage and liberation.
items.inference: Even while unchanging, Śiva is the cause of bondage and liberation for individual selves.
items.plain_english: Even while unchanging, Śiva is the cause of bondage and liberation for individual selves.

rows.grounds: by coming together or ripening together

items.question: What causes Śiva's power to descend upon the individual self?
premises: Two karmas come into conjunction.
Śiva's power is capable of descending.
The individual self is the locus of this descent.
items.inference: By the conjunction of the two karmas, Śiva's power falls upon the individual self.
uncertainties: The specific identity of the two karmas is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: By the conjunction of the two karmas, Śiva's power descends upon the individual self.

rows.grounds: of the power that bestows grace

items.question: When does the descent of the grace-bestowing power occur for the individual self?
premises: Experience leads to the ripening of impurity.
Impurity becomes ripe at a certain stage.
Grace-bestowing power descends when conditions are ready.
items.inference: When impurity is ripened through experience, the descent of the grace-bestowing power occurs.
uncertainties: The exact referent of the editorial marker ||(6|19 is unclear.
items.plain_english: Through experience, when impurity is ripened, there is the descent of the grace-bestowing power.

rows.grounds: whose impurity and stain have been calmed

items.question: What does one perceive when the impurity and stain of the self are pacified?
premises: Impurity and stain can become pacified.
The self is the object of perception.
Pacification alters how the self is seen.
items.inference: One perceives the self whose impurity and stain have been pacified.
items.plain_english: One perceives the self whose impurity and stain have been pacified.

rows.grounds: because the covering of impurity has departed
nature consisting of omniscience and other qualities

items.question: What becomes manifest in the self when the covering of impurity is removed?
premises: Impurity functions as a covering over the self.
Removal of that covering frees the self from it.
The self's nature includes omniscience and other qualities.
items.inference: When the covering of impurity is removed, the self's nature of omniscience and other qualities shines forth.
items.plain_english: The meaning is that, by the removal of the covering of impurity, this self's nature of omniscience and so on, freed from that, shines forth.

rows.grounds: by regular and occasional rites or actions

items.question: How does this one abide supremely through daily and occasional action?
premises: Daily and occasional actions are prescribed.
The subject continues to act by means of them.
Such action is associated with a supreme mode of abiding.
items.inference: This one abides supremely by means of daily and occasional action.
items.plain_english: This one abides supremely by means of daily and occasional action.
